papers.title: Machine-learning-based neutrino-event generation constrained by experimental measurements
papers.abstract: We present a generative surrogate for charged-current \(\nu_\mu\)-nucleus scattering that can be calibrated to measured differential cross sections without event-level experimental samples. Starting from a theoretical interaction model, we fine-tune the surrogate to a MicroBooNE measurement and show that this also improves the description of observables not used in the fit. The calibrated model can also be applied to measurements from different neutrino fluxes without retuning, while retaining event-level predictions of outgoing-muon kinematics. Our results show that experimental cross sections can directly constrain generative event models while preserving their applicability across different observables and beam configurations.
papers.reason: Presents a generative surrogate for neutrino-nucleus scattering calibrated directly against MicroBooNE data, hitting core generator and cross-section interests.

summary.tldr: A generative surrogate for $\nu_\mu$-nucleus scattering combines a cross-section DNN and cGAN, enabling calibration directly to unfolded, smeared MicroBooNE differential cross sections via differentiable histogramming without event-level experimental data.
summary.novel_idea: Bridges the gap between published binned differential cross sections and event-by-event Monte Carlo simulation without requiring detector response inversion. It introduces an adversarial data-informed 'reservoir' regularization step to prevent kinematic mode collapse, paired with a differentiable sigmoid-based soft-histogramming layer to optimize the generator and cross-section normalizer directly against full measurement covariance matrices.
summary.method: Trained on 20 million CC $\nu_\mu$-argon events from NuWro across $E_\nu \in [0.11, 20]$~GeV to construct a base conditional GAN and a $\sigma$-DNN. Fine-tuning uses a two-step framework: an adversarial loss using a 1-million-event reservoir drawn according to MicroBooNE 3D differential cross-section occupancies, followed by differentiable soft binning forward-smeared by the MicroBooNE detector matrix $A_c$ to minimize a full-covariance $\chi^2$. Generalization is tested out-of-training on independent MicroBooNE and ArgoNeuT measurements.
key_results: Calibrates NuWro-based cGAN kinematics to MicroBooNE $d^2\sigma/dp_\mu d\cos\theta_\mu$ bins of $E_\nu$, significantly reducing data-MC $\chi^2$ compared to the untuned base model.
Accurately predicts independent, out-of-training MicroBooNE observables including $d\sigma/dE_{\rm had}$, $d\sigma/dE_\mu$, and $\sigma/\langle E_\nu \rangle$.
Demonstrates flux portability by successfully predicting ArgoNeuT differential cross sections in both neutrino and antineutrino beam configurations without retuning.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to neutrino event generator development (NuWro, GENIE, Achilles) and generator-tuning methodologies. Provides a concrete, differentiable ML surrogate architecture that allows generators to assimilate binned LArTPC cross sections directly while preserving physical event-level phase space.
summary.caveats: Currently restricted to outgoing muon kinematics $(p_\mu, \cos\theta_\mu)$ without modeling correlated hadronic final states, nuclear remnants, or FSI. Reservoir construction uses absolute values for unfolded bins with negative central values, although the subsequent fit retains full signed covariances.

papers.title: Gallium Anomaly and Solar Neutrinos
papers.abstract: The Gallium Anomaly is the disagreement between the measured capture rate of neutrinos by $^{71}$Ga and the rate theoretically expected from the electron capture decay of $^{71}$Ge. The experimental measurements were performed with intense artificial sources. In the present work we consider the sun as a neutrino source that can be calibrated via the fundamental, standard-model neutrino-electron elastic scattering reaction in terrestrial detectors. The result is found to be not anomalous, with good agreement between the measured value of $66.1\pm3.1$ SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO, and the total measured source strengths of solar sources, $67.5^{+1.4}_{-1.1}$ SNU. It may be concluded that neither the $^{71}$Ga charged-current cross section nor gallium experiment extraction and counting efficiencies account for the Gallium Anomaly.
papers.reason: Re-evaluates the Gallium anomaly using the Sun as a calibrated neutrino source via elastic scattering, directly addressing a core low-energy neutrino anomaly.

summary.tldr: Calibrating the solar neutrino flux with elastic scattering and SNO neutral-current measurements yields a predicted $^{71}\text{Ga}$ rate matching Gallex/SAGE, showing the Gallium Anomaly does not stem from cross sections or detection efficiencies.
summary.novel_idea: Uses terrestrial solar neutrino measurements (Borexino ES and SNO NC) along with the solar luminosity constraint to test the $^{71}\text{Ga}$ charged-current capture rate independently of solar interior models. This directly confronts claims that electron-nucleus wavefunction non-factorization reduces the $^{71}\text{Ga}(\nu_e, e^-)^{71}\text{Ge}$ cross section derived via detailed balance.
summary.method: Determines the solar $\nu_e$ flux components ($pp$ from the solar luminosity constraint, $^7\text{Be}$, $pep$, $\text{CNO}$ from Borexino, and $^8\text{B}$ from SNO) and folds them with standard MSW matter survival probabilities ($P_{ee}$) using the MB22p solar model density profiles. Evaluates capture rates using updated ground-state Gamow-Teller matrix elements anchored by detailed balance to the precisely measured $^{71}\text{Ge}$ electron capture half-life ($11.465$ days) and excited states from $(p,n)$ data.
key_results: The predicted solar neutrino capture rate on $^{71}\text{Ga}$ is $67.5^{+1.4}_{-1.1}$~SNU, in excellent agreement with the Gallex/GNO and SAGE measured value of $66.1 \pm 3.1$~SNU (ratio $0.980^{+0.050}_{-0.049}$).
Over 90% of the calculated solar rate in gallium is driven by the ground-state transition anchored by detailed balance.
Refutes hypotheses that a $\sim 20\%$ breakdown of electron-nuclear wavefunction factorization accounts for the Gallium Anomaly.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts low-energy charged-current neutrino-nucleus interactions, radiochemical extraction benchmarks, and Gamow-Teller transition matrix element calculations relevant to stopped-pion and solar/supernova neutrino detection. Reinforces that the radioactive source deficit (BEST anomaly) points elsewhere than standard cross-section modeling.
summary.caveats: Does not explain the physical origin of the $\sim 4\sigma$ deficit observed in intense artificial source experiments ($^{51}\text{Cr}, ^{37}\text{Ar}$). Relies on standard solar MSW survival probabilities being free from unknown short-baseline sterile oscillations.

papers.title: DUNE Beam-Energy Dependence of Sensitivity to the Violation of the Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the dependence of DUNE's sensitivity to possible violations of the equivalence principle (VEP) on the beam-energy configuration, comparing the Low-Energy (LE) and Medium-Energy (ME) beams. We find that the LE configuration generally provides stronger constraints on the VEP parameters than the ME configuration. For $\theta_{23}=43^\circ$, the LE configuration constrains $\Phi\Delta\gamma_{21}$ and $\Phi\Delta\gamma_{31}$ to $8.47\times10^{-24}$ and $8.53\times10^{-24}$, respectively, at the $3\sigma$ CL. The appearance channels shows stronger phase-dependency degeneracies while the disappearance channels exhibits smoother exclusion sensitivity. This work further confirms the advantage of the LE configuration over the ME, in constraining the correlated VEP parameter space. For the assumed true value of $\theta_{23}=43^\circ$, The LE configuration restricts the VEP parameter space to $\mathit{\Phi}\Delta\gamma_{21}\in[-8.47,\,8.47]\times10^{-24}$ and $\mathit{\Phi}\Delta\gamma_{31}\in[-8.53,\,8.53]\times10^{-24}$ at $3\sigma$.We also find that neutrino-mode and antineutrino-mode running can independently probe VEP effects at DUNE, with the relative sensitivity depending on the beam-energy configuration. These results highlight the importance of beam-energy optimization and channel-wise analysis in exploring possible violations of the equivalence principle at DUNE.
papers.reason: Evaluates DUNE's sensitivity to violations of the equivalence principle (VEP) comparing low-energy and medium-energy beam configurations, directly relevant to DUNE oscillation systematics.

summary.tldr: A DUNE simulation demonstrates that the Low-Energy beam tune provides superior sensitivity to violations of the equivalence principle over the Medium-Energy tune by concentrating statistics at the first oscillation maximum.
summary.novel_idea: Systematically analyzes the sensitivity of DUNE to violations of the equivalence principle (VEP) in the $(2,3)$ gravitational sector as a function of beam-energy configuration. It shows that despite the linear energy growth of the VEP Hamiltonian term ($\propto E$), the Low-Energy (LE) beam tune outperforms the Medium-Energy (ME) tune due to tighter spectral alignment with the primary oscillation maximum.
summary.method: Modifies the three-flavor neutrino propagation Hamiltonian in GLoBES to include weak-field static gravitational potential couplings ($t_1 = \Phi\Delta\gamma_{21}$ and $t_2 = \Phi\Delta\gamma_{31}$). Simulates a 40~kton Far Detector with 1300~km baseline over a 13-year exposure ($6.5~\text{yr FHC} + 6.5~\text{yr RHC}$) using GEANT4/G4LBNF LE and ME fluxes, marginalizing over standard oscillation parameters, VEP phases, and matter density.
key_results: For $\theta_{23} = 43^\circ$, the LE configuration constrains $|\Phi\Delta\gamma_{21}| < 8.47 \times 10^{-24}$ and $|\Phi\Delta\gamma_{31}| < 8.53 \times 10^{-24}$ at $3\sigma$ CL, outperforming the ME bound ($1.15 \times 10^{-23}$).

Appearance channels ($\nu_e, \bar{\nu}_e$) exhibit significant parameter degeneracies between standard $\delta_{\rm CP}$ and exotic VEP CP phase $\Phi_N$, producing non-monotonic $\Delta\chi^2$ sensitivity profiles.
Disappearance channels ($\nu_\mu, \bar{\nu}_\mu$) show smooth, monotonic $\Delta\chi^2$ increases, anchoring the statistical bounds at the $10^{-23}$ scale.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides context on beam optimization and exotic oscillation phenomenology at DUNE. However, it relies entirely on parameterized detector smearing without addressing interaction systematics, nucleon form factors, or nuclear cross sections.
summary.caveats: Restricts gravitational mixing strictly to the $(2,3)$ sector with $t_2 = 0$ in single-parameter marginalizations. Does not incorporate detailed nuclear modeling systematics or event-generator mismodeling effects.

papers.title: $^6$He structure from semiclassical 3D models based on $\textit{ab initio}$ spatial correlations
papers.abstract: We construct semiclassical 3D models based on $\textit{ab initio}$ no-core shell model calculated two-body spatial correlations, which represent the preferred spatial configuration of nucleons for the ground state of $^6$He. We demonstrate that the presence of the two valence neutrons distorts and flattens the $\alpha$ core in $^6$He, marking a clear departure from the tetrahedral configuration of free $^4$He, and that the two valence neutrons and the center of mass of the $\alpha$ cluster ($\alpha$-CM) are roughly located at the three distinct vertices of an equilateral triangle. We compute the geometric parameters that commonly characterize $^6$He structure, 1) $\theta_{nn}$, the opening angle of the two valence neutrons with respect to $\alpha$-CM, and 2) $r_{nn}$, the root-mean-square separation between the two valence neutrons. Refining the model with uncertainty estimation, we obtain $\theta_{nn}= 58.5^{+5.4}_{-6.2}$ degrees and $r_{nn}= 4.12^{+0.37}_{-0.43}$ fm, agreeing with those calculated via a phenomenologically modified continuum-discretized coupled-channels method, while an interferometry experiment obtained a marginally higher $r_{nn}$.
papers.reason: Constructs semiclassical 3D models of 6He based on ab initio spatial correlations, examining alpha-core distortion and valence neutron geometry with direct nuclear-structure relevance.

summary.tldr: Semiclassical 3D geometric models based on ab initio no-core shell model two-body spatial correlations reveal that the $\alpha$ core of $^6\text{He}$ is significantly flattened by valence halo neutrons.
summary.novel_idea: Constructs semiclassical 3D spatial configurations of halo nuclei directly from ab initio two-body spatial correlation operators ($r^0$ pair-number and $r^2$ separation) computed with the No-Core Shell Model (NCSM). It demonstrates that the presence of halo neutrons distorts the $\alpha$ core away from the tetrahedral shape of free $^4\text{He}$ into an almost planar geometry.
summary.method: Computes rotationally invariant, spin- and isospin-projected two-body expectation values in NCSM using the Daejeon16 $NN$ interaction at $N_{\rm max}=16$ and $\hbar\Omega=10$~MeV. Sets up systems of nonlinear equations for inter-nucleon distances for the dominant two-body spin configuration, introducing a semiclassical parameter $\xi$ to delineate core-valence from valence-valence correlations and estimate uncertainty.
key_results: Determines an opening angle of the two valence neutrons relative to the $\alpha$-CM of $\theta_{nn} = 58.5^{+5.4}_{-6.2}$ degrees, forming a near-equilateral triangle with the core.
Finds an rms separation between the valence neutrons of $r_{nn} = 4.12^{+0.37}_{-0.43}$~fm, agreeing with phenomenological continuum-discretized coupled-channels (CDCC) results.
Demonstrates that the $\alpha$ core inside $^6\text{He}$ is squeezed into a nearly planar configuration, whereas free $^4\text{He}$ remains tetrahedral under the same procedure.
summary.why_it_matters: Interesting methodology for interpreting spatial nucleon-nucleon correlations from ab initio shell-model wavefunctions, but focused on $^6\text{He}$ rather than argon, carbon, or oxygen targets relevant to neutrino scattering.
summary.caveats: Relies on a semiclassical 'snapshot' interpretation of quantum two-body densities. The uncertainty interval is derived from heuristic physical criteria imposed on the semiclassical parameter $\xi$.

papers.title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
papers.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_\mu^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_\mu^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.
authors: A. De Santis (Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration)
papers.reason: Provides a precise lattice QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic vacuum polarization for the muon g-2 using twisted-mass fermions, highly relevant to lattice and Standard Model precision.

summary.tldr: ETMC reports a high-precision lattice QCD determination of the leading-order hadronic vacuum polarization in isospin-symmetric QCD, yielding $a_\mu^{\rm HVP} = (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$, consistent with the Fermilab $(g-2)_\mu$ measurement.
summary.novel_idea: Presents an independent $\sim 1\%$ first-principles determination of the isospin-symmetric hadronic vacuum polarization using Wilson-clover twisted-mass fermions. Crucially, it evaluates and reconciles results across two distinct scale-setting prescriptions: the FLAG scheme ($f_\pi$-based) and the WP25 scheme ($w_0$-based).
summary.method: Evaluates the vector-vector correlator via the time-momentum representation on $N_f = 2+1+1$ ensembles at physical pion mass, four lattice spacings ($a \simeq 0.049\text{--}0.079$~fm), and box sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm. Implements blinded analyses with twisted-mass and Osterwalder-Seiler regularizations taking a combined continuum limit, and corrects finite-volume effects using two spatial volumes alongside an MLLGS two-pion model.
key_results: Obtains $a_\mu^{\rm HVP}(\text{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9)\times 10^{-10}$ in the FLAG scheme and $(714.8 \pm 7.4)\times 10^{-10}$ in the WP25 scheme.
Combining with WP25 isospin-breaking corrections yields $a_\mu^{\rm HVP} = (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$, making the SM prediction fully compatible with the BNL+Fermilab experimental average.
Confirms high-precision agreement across lattice groups in the intermediate Euclidean-time window while reinforcing the $2.4\sigma$ tension with pre-CMD-3 dispersive data.
summary.why_it_matters: A landmark lattice QCD result for the muon $g-2$ puzzle, but peripheral to your focus on neutrino-nucleus interactions, nucleon axial/vector form factors, and electroweak nuclear response.
summary.caveats: Isospin-breaking corrections are not yet computed directly from first principles by ETMC and are taken from the WP25 average. Twisted-mass neutral/charged pion mass splittings at finite lattice spacing require explicit MLLGS modeling rather than model-independent spectral reconstruction.

papers.title: Leptogenesis with a GeV-Scale Quasi-Dirac Neutrino
papers.abstract: We discuss leptogenesis in a model with a GeV-scale quasi-Dirac neutral lepton, comprising mainly sterile states, which is accessible to future experiments. In particular, we show that Higgs-decay leptogenesis can naturally arise from the type-I seesaw mechanism with spontaneously broken global lepton number together with a discrete $Z_2$ symmetry, yielding two quasi-degenerate right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) which, to excellent approximation, form a single Dirac neutrino, with a tiny mass splitting as required for resonant enhancement generated by higher-dimensional lepton-number-violating operators. Incorporating finite-temperature effects, we show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully generated through thermal Higgs decays for 0.1-10 GeV mass quasi-Dirac neutrinos, with the CP asymmetry arising from the interplay between the vacuum and thermal contributions to the mass splitting. In the parameter region of successful leptogenesis, the quasi-Dirac neutrino is accessible to future heavy neutral lepton searches at SHiP, MATHUSLA and FCC-ee. In addition, the same symmetry-breaking sector gives rise to unstable domain walls whose annihilation can generate a stochastic gravitational-wave background, providing a complementary probe of the framework.
papers.reason: Explores Higgs-decay leptogenesis via GeV-scale quasi-Dirac sterile neutrinos testable at SHiP and FCC-ee, connecting closely to high-priority HNL interests.

summary.tldr: Thermal Higgs decays ($H\to LN$) in the early Universe generate the baryon asymmetry via GeV-scale quasi-Dirac neutrinos with symmetry-protected mass splitting, testable at SHiP, MATHUSLA, and FCC-ee.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike standard resonant leptogenesis or ARS oscillations, this framework achieves low-scale leptogenesis for sub-electroweak scale RHNs ($0.1\text{--}10\text{ GeV}$) via thermal Higgs decays ($H \to LN$) before sphaleron freeze-out. The required tiny mass splitting emerges naturally from higher-dimensional $U(1)_L$-breaking operators in a $U(1)_L \times Z_2$ seesaw model rather than ad hoc parameter tuning.
summary.method: The authors solve coupled Boltzmann equations for the $B-L$ yield in the narrow temperature window between electroweak symmetry breaking ($T_c \sim 160\text{ GeV}$) and sphaleron decoupling ($T_{\rm sph} \simeq 131.7\text{ GeV}$). The CP asymmetry is purely thermal in origin, calculated from the interference between tree and thermal-loop Higgs decay amplitudes. The viable parameter space is mapped to active-sterile mixing $|\theta_e|^2$ and compared directly against limits and projections for SHiP, MATHUSLA, and FCC-ee.
key_results: The observed baryon asymmetry is successfully reproduced for quasi-Dirac neutrino masses $M_N \in [0.1, 10]\text{ GeV}$ with vacuum mass splittings $\Delta M^0 \sim 10^{-10}\text{--}10^{-8}\text{ GeV}$.

The parameter space yielding successful leptogenesis requires active-sterile mixing $|\theta_e|^2 \sim 10^{-9}\text{--}10^{-6}$ for $M_N \sim 0.5\text{--}5\text{ GeV}$, lying right within the discovery reach of SHiP and MATHUSLA via displaced decays.
Spontaneous $Z_2$ breaking generates domain walls whose annihilation via dimension-5 bias operators produces a stochastic gravitational wave background observable by LISA, ET, and DECIGO.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly connects to the reader's interest in BSM neutrino portals and heavy neutral lepton (HNL) searches at intensity-frontier experiments such as SHiP. It provides a concrete low-scale seesaw benchmark tying early-Universe leptogenesis directly to laboratory HNL displaced-vertex phenomenology.
summary.caveats: Assumes a negligible initial RHN abundance before the electroweak phase transition, and the accompanying Majoron cannot simultaneously account for the dark matter abundance while satisfying cosmological stability bounds.

papers.title: Nuclear PDFs
papers.abstract: We summarize the current status of global analyses of model-independent nuclear parton distri- bution functions (nPDFs). A carefully conducted global analysis of nPDFs in the era of heavy-ion collisions at the LHC is key to gaining access to new information through the data measured by the collider experiments. This implies incorporating as large and diverse a dataset as possible, as well as the latest theoretical calculations, in order to capture a faithful representation of nuclear structure that reflects the current state of knowledge. On the other hand, the uncertainties in par- ticular must reflect what is not known. For many observables, nuclear uncertainties represent the most significant source of error in current theoretical models; nevertheless, they should not, where possible, be artificially constrained (for example, through parameterization bias). The quality of a global (n)PDF fit is often measured by the $\chi^2$ per degree of freedom, which is approximately one for a fit that describes the data precisely without overfitting. Many additional aspects allow to characterize a good fit, e.g. the $\chi^2$ distribution per experiment, the shape of the uncertainties, and the sensitivity to different types of data. We inspect various fit quality indicators for fits obtained by different groups. Morever we pay close attention to the $A$-dependence. Traditionally, the A-dependence had a primarily functional role in global nPDF analyses and comparatively less attention has been paid to it when characterizing a fit. However, we have now entered the era of nuclei collisions at the LHC and need to investigate the $A$-dependence properly.
papers.reason: Comprehensive review of global analyses of model-independent nuclear PDFs, critical for reducing interaction systematic uncertainties in accelerator neutrino experiments.

summary.tldr: Global NLO analyses of nuclear PDFs (nCTEQ26 preliminary, EPPS21, nNNPDF3.0) and NNLO TUJU21 are systematically compared, highlighting data sensitivities, strange-sea constraints from neutrino DIS, and $A$-dependent uncertainty patterns.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first comparative benchmark incorporating preliminary nCTEQ26 results alongside EPPS21 and nNNPDF3.0, focusing specifically on how diverse experimental datasets and functional parameterizations dictate the nuclear mass number ($A$) dependence of uncertainties.
summary.method: Compares global NLO fits across neutral-current DIS, charged-current neutrino DIS, dimuon production (NuTeV/CCFR), and LHC hadron collider data ($W/Z$, dijets, heavy flavor). Analyzes nuclear modification factors $R_i^A(x, Q^2)$ and evaluates uncertainty bands using Hessian (nCTEQ, EPPS) versus Monte Carlo replica (nNNPDF) approaches across $A$ from deuteron to lead.
key_results: All three NLO collaborations show strong convergence for valence quark distributions ($u_v, d_v$), but exhibit substantial discrepancies in the strange sea and low-$x$ gluons.
nCTEQ26 achieves significantly reduced strange-quark uncertainties near iron ($A=56$) due to the inclusion of NuTeV and CCFR neutrino-scattering dimuon data.

nNNPDF3.0 yields a flavour-democratic light sea ($\bar{u} \approx \bar{d} \approx s$), whereas EPPS21 and nCTEQ26 show a suppressed strange sea consistent with strange-mass thresholds in neutrino DIS.
nCTEQ26 achieves the smallest low-$x$ gluon uncertainty for lead ($A=208$) owing to extensive LHC heavy-quark production datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly hits core interests in neutrino-nucleus deep-inelastic scattering and generator development (e.g., GENIE, GiBUU DIS regimes). Understanding how neutrino DIS dimuon data constrain the nuclear strange sea versus LHC collider data is vital for precision modeling of high-energy neutrino cross sections and oscillation systematics.
summary.caveats: Light nuclei remain poorly constrained due to limited data, and differing treatments of deuteron corrections introduce baseline discrepancies between collaborations.

papers.title: Low-Scale See-Saw Mechanism and the Majorana Nature of Heavy Neutrinos
papers.abstract: We investigate the possibility to determine the Majorana nature of the heavy Majorana neutrinos present in the low-scale type I seesaw mechanism of neutrino mass generation in experiments at $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $\mu^+ \text{-} \mu^-$ colliders. This is done on the examples of two specific symmetry-protected seesaw scenarios with two right-handed (RH) singlet neutrinos and one seesaw realization with three RH neutrinos. We use the forward-backward symmetry in the angular distribution of the heavy neutral leptons produced in the $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $\mu^+ \text{-} \mu^-$ collisions as an indicator of their Majorana nature. Our results indicate that the experiments at FCCee during its first phase of operation have a remarkable potential not only to discover the heavy neutral leptons associated with the type I seesaw mechanism if they have masses smaller than the $Z^0$-boson mass, but also to probe and provide evidence for their Majorana nature.
papers.reason: Explores forward-backward asymmetry signatures at lepton colliders (FCC-ee) to probe the Majorana nature of low-scale type-I seesaw heavy neutral leptons.

summary.tldr: Heavy neutral leptons in low-scale type-I seesaw models can reveal their Majorana or Dirac nature at future $e^+e^-$ and $\mu^+\mu^-$ colliders via forward-backward angular distribution asymmetries.
summary.novel_idea: Demonstrates that forward-backward asymmetry ($A_{\rm FB}$) in $e^+e^- (\mu^+\mu^-) \to N + \nu \to l^- + 2j + E_{\rm miss}$ can distinguish Majorana from Dirac HNLs even in realistic multi-RHN seesaw realizations (two pseudo-Dirac or three hierarchical RHNs), resolving pseudo-Dirac mass degeneracies without demanding direct lepton-number violation tagging.
summary.method: Analytically computes lepton-number-conserving (LNC) and lepton-number-violating (LNV) differential cross sections mediated by $W^\pm$ and $Z^0$ intermediate states for $e^+e^- \to N_j \nu \to l^- W^+ \nu \to l^- j_1 j_2 E_{\rm miss}$. Evaluates $d\sigma/d\cos\theta$ and $A_{\rm FB}$ at the $Z$-pole ($\sqrt{s}=M_Z$) and $\sqrt{s}=350\text{ GeV}$ under varying reconstructed mass resolutions $\delta M_{l j_1 j_2}$.
key_results: Majorana HNL production satisfies exact forward-backward symmetry ($A_{\rm FB} = 0$) due to the cancellation between LNC and LNV angular terms, whereas pure Dirac production exhibits a pronounced non-zero asymmetry ($A_{\rm FB} \neq 0$).

For two quasi-degenerate RHNs with tiny mass splitting ($|M_2 - M_1| \ll \Gamma$), production mimics a Dirac fermion ($A_{\rm FB} \approx 0.127$ at $M_N = 60\text{ GeV}$), but transitions to an effective Majorana signature ($A_{\rm FB} \approx 0$) at lower masses ($M_N = 10\text{ GeV}$).
FCC-ee running at the $Z$-pole ($6 \times 10^{12}$ $Z$ bosons) has sufficient statistics to resolve multiple HNL resonant Breit-Wigner peaks and test their Majorana nature through angular profiling.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly connects to high-priority interests in HNL phenomenology, future collider neutrino physics (FCC-ee, muon colliders), and spin/angular correlations in leptonic scattering final states.
summary.caveats: The study does not include detector acceptance cuts, finite jet reconstruction efficiencies, or full Standard Model background simulations; dedicated experimental feasibility studies remain to be performed.

papers.title: Identification of ultra-high-energy neutrinos in vertical air showers with surface detectors
papers.abstract: We investigate the potential of surface detector arrays to identify ultra-high-energy neutrinos using vertical air showers with zenith angle $\theta \leq 60^\circ$, a region largely unexplored in current searches. The method exploits the enhanced electromagnetic component at ground level arising from energetic leptons produced in neutrino interactions. Using detailed air-shower and detector simulations, we show that observables sensitive to the electromagnetic and muonic content provide genuine discrimination between neutrino-induced and hadron-induced showers. This is demonstrated both with idealized shower quantities and with realistic detector-level signals based on water-Cherenkov and scintillator detectors. The corresponding neutrino identification efficiency is used to derive the effective mass and, primarily, the effective area of the array under background-rejection requirements appropriate to targeted multi-messenger searches. Although not competitive with inclined-shower searches under the stringent background rejection factors required for diffuse-flux analyses, this approach establishes the feasibility of a vertical detection channel, extending the field of view of surface arrays and providing a complementary tool for multi-messenger observations of transient sources.
papers.reason: Investigates surface detector identification of ultra-high-energy neutrinos via vertical air showers, directly relevant to neutrino observatory techniques and background rejection.

summary.tldr: Surface detector arrays can identify vertical ($\theta \leq 60^\circ$) ultra-high-energy electron-neutrino air showers around $10^{18}\text{ eV}$ by separating electromagnetic and muonic signals using combined water-Cherenkov and scintillator detectors.
summary.novel_idea: Extends UHE neutrino searches in surface arrays to vertical zenith angles ($\theta \leq 60^\circ$), previously neglected due to intense cosmic-ray backgrounds, by exploiting the elevated ratio of electromagnetic to muonic ground signals in deep CC $\nu_e$ showers for targeted multi-messenger alerts.
summary.method: Simulates $10^{18}\text{ eV}$ air showers using CORSIKA (EPOS-LHC + FLUKA) and neutrino interactions via HERWIG at $\theta = 30^\circ$, combined with a Geant4 model of a 1500 m-spaced array mimicking Pierre Auger/AugerPrime (WCD + SSD). Applies Fisher discriminant analysis to the recorded signals $S_{\rm WCD}$ and $S_{\rm SSD}$ at 1000 m from the core to determine tagging efficiency, effective mass, and effective area.
key_results: Reaches an effective area of $A_{\rm eff} \simeq 1.6 \times 10^{-2}\text{ km}^2$ for $\nu_e$ at $10^{18}\text{ eV}$ and $\theta = 30^\circ$ at a background rejection factor of $\varepsilon_{\rm bkg} = 2 \times 10^{-5}$ (ideal Monte Carlo observables reach $4.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ km}^2$).
Demonstrates that discrimination is driven almost entirely by charged-current $\nu_e$ interactions, where $70\text{--}80\%$ of primary energy enters the electromagnetic shower.

Vertical channel diffuse-flux sensitivity at $\theta \in [30^\circ, 35^\circ]$ is $\sim 15$ times weaker than current Auger inclined limits, but competitive for transient multi-messenger sources within tight temporal windows.
summary.why_it_matters: Largely tangential to the reader's primary focus on microscopic neutrino-nucleus cross sections and accelerator/low-energy experiments. However, it offers context for high-energy cosmic neutrino detection techniques using hybrid surface detectors.
summary.caveats: Simulations are restricted to a single energy ($10^{18}\text{ eV}$) and fixed angle ($\theta = 30^\circ$), assume a simplified station trigger threshold, and cannot distinguish $\nu_e$ showers from primary gamma-ray cascades.

papers.title: Extracting the Central Sound Speed of Neutron Stars through Intrinsic Stellar Structure Scaling with Reduced Equation-of-State Model Dependence
papers.abstract: Inferring neutron star (NS) core properties remains sensitive to the assumed equation of state (EOS). Using a nonlinear Walecka model with generalized $\omega$-meson self-interactions, we construct six EOS families, each containing $10^3$ samples subject to identical nuclear and astrophysical constraints. Despite satisfying these constraints, the families predict markedly different high-density behavior and core properties; higher-order $\omega$ interactions can also generate interior sound-speed peaks within purely nucleonic matter. To reduce this model dependence, we use the intrinsic and perturbative analysis of the dimensionless Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations (IPAD-TOV) to derive an EOS-independent estimator $\Theta(\rm{X},\Psi)$ of the central squared sound speed $s_{\rm c}^2$, where $\rm{X}=P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ is the central EOS-parameter and $\Psi$ characterizes the stellar-mass response to central energy density. For canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NSs, $\Theta$ correlates linearly with $s_{\rm c}^2$ across the families ($R^2\approx0.94$-$0.99$). The family-dependent relations converge toward a common optimum: minimizing their dispersion yields $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.523\pm0.044$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.173^{+0.020}_{-0.018}$ for all six families, or $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.496\pm0.092$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.167^{+0.030}_{-0.029}$ when the family without $\omega$ self-interaction is excluded. The corresponding radii are $11.73^{+1.08}_{-0.92}$ and $11.92^{+1.76}_{-1.28}\,\rm km$, respectively, with $95\%$ confidence intervals. A unified scaling fitted to all EOS samples supports both extractions. These results show how common stellar-structure relations can constrain NS core properties with reduced EOS-model dependence, even when existing observations cannot distinguish among the underlying EOS descriptions.
papers.reason: Derives EOS-independent estimators for central sound speeds in neutron stars, highly relevant to nuclear matter equations of state and high-density nuclear physics.

summary.tldr: Intrinsic perturbative TOV scaling yields an EOS-independent estimator for the central sound speed of canonical neutron stars, constraining $s_{\rm c}^2 \approx 0.52$ and radius $\approx 11.7\text{ km}$ across diverse nonlinear Walecka models.
summary.novel_idea: Develops a sub-leading order expansion in the dimensionless TOV framework (IPAD-TOV) to construct an analytical estimator $\Theta(X, \Psi)$ for the central sound speed squared ($s_c^2$), demonstrating that minimizing dispersion among diverse EOS families isolates common core properties with reduced EOS model dependence.
summary.method: Constructs six ensembles of 1000 EOSs each using generalized nonlinear Walecka relativistic mean-field models with varying $\omega$-meson self-interactions ($\omega^{2q}$, $q=3/2$ to $5$, and $c_\omega=0$), constrained by saturation properties, MBPT, NICER, and GW170817. Derives dimensionless TOV expansions about the stellar center connecting central stiffness $X=P_c/\varepsilon_c$ and mass-energy response $\Psi$ to $s_c^2$.
key_results: Nonlinear $\omega$ self-interactions naturally generate an interior sound-speed peak within purely nucleonic matter without requiring a deconfinement phase transition.
The estimator $\Theta(X, \Psi)$ correlates tightly with true central $s_c^2$ across all six families ($R^2 \approx 0.94\text{--}0.99$).

Minimizing inter-family dispersion for canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NSs extracts $s_c^2 \approx 0.523 \pm 0.044$, $X \approx 0.173^{+0.020}_{-0.018}$, and radius $R_{1.4} \approx 11.73^{+1.08}_{-0.92}\text{ km}$ (95% CI), well above the conformal limit $s_c^2 = 1/3$.
summary.why_it_matters: Tangential to theoretical neutrino-nucleus scattering and generator physics. It may be of minor interest only for background knowledge on relativistic mean-field theory formulations and dense nuclear matter symmetry energy behavior.
summary.caveats: The scaling extraction is tested only within classes of generalized Walecka RMF models and assumes the absence of sharp first-order phase transitions in the core.

papers.title: The Sill distribution for all partial waves
papers.abstract: In high-energy physics, short-lived resonances appearing in scattering processes are described by energy-dependent spectral functions. The relativistic Breit--Wigner distribution (rBW), obtained as a relativistic extension of the standard Breit--Wigner form, is commonly employed owing to its simplicity. However, when the lower-energy threshold lies sufficiently close to the resonance peak, sizable deviations from the rBW line shape are expected. The Sill distribution provides a simple way to incorporate the physical threshold while preserving exact normalization, but in its original formulation it is inherently restricted to $s$-wave decays. Here, we extend the Sill distribution to arbitrary partial waves. The correct $\ell$-wave threshold behaviour is implemented while exact normalization is retained through a simple modification of the mass term of the propagator. As a benchmark, the $p$-wave Sill provides a very good description of the $\Delta(1232)^{++}$ line shape up to 1.35 GeV and simultaneously reproduces its on-shell mass and width and its complex pole position, in agreement with independent determinations compiled by the PDG.
papers.reason: Extends the Sill resonance line-shape distribution to arbitrary partial waves with proper threshold behavior, successfully benchmarking against the Delta(1232) pole.

papers.title: Disentangling geometry & growth in cosmic neutrino mass constraints: a more physical split and diagnostic
papers.abstract:
Recent cosmological data hint at a neutrino mass sum below the minimum value allowed by the neutrino mass oscillation experiments, with a preference for the opposite of massive neutrinos ("negative" neutrino masses). Since massive neutrinos impact the expansion history of the Universe, which in turn modifies the growth of structure, we ask whether such a preference originates from the observed geometry or structure growth, and whether the two agree. In this paper, we introduce a more physical split of $\sum m_
u$ into parameters $\sum m_
u^{geo}$ and $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ based on their physical effects, with extension to negative values. We split the expansion rate at the Boltzmann-code level: $\sum m_
u^{geo}$ sets $H(z)$ for distance computation, and $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ sets $H(z)$ for perturbation evolution. Combining Planck primary CMB, Planck+ACT+SPT CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, we find similar sensitivity and "negative" preference from geometry and growth with $\sum m_
u^{geo} = -0.07\pm0.10$ eV (68% C.L.) and $\sum m_
u^{growth} = -0.13^{+0.10}_{-0.12}$ eV (68% C.L.). The difference of the two is a null test of the $\Lambda$CDM model, passed by current data at $0.4\sigma$ level. Forecasts on Advanced SO CMB and DESI DR3 BAO show that $0.058$ eV would be rejected at $3.0\sigma$ from the geometry channel alone, if the negative mean of $\sum m_
u^{geo} = -0.07$ eV persists. The two channels can also provide a powerful new diagnostic between possible origins of the neutrino mass tension. With future CMB and BAO data, our Fisher forecasts show that an incorrect dark energy model displaces $\sum m_
u^{geo}$ from $0.058$ eV by $3.1$-$4.2\sigma$ and $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ by $1.1$-$1.3\sigma$, while an underestimated reionization optical depth reverses the pattern, $2.7$-$3.6\sigma$ in $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ against at most $0.23\sigma$ in $\sum m_
u^{geo}$. (Abridged)
papers.reason: Disentangles geometry and growth in cosmological constraints on neutrino mass sums, offering relevant context for global oscillation and mass analyses.

papers.title: Stimulated capture of axion dark matter around primordial black holes
papers.abstract: We study the stimulated capture of axion and axion-like particles around primordial black holes, mediated by quartic self-interactions. We identify the parametric regions where Bose-enhanced growth overcomes cosmological dilution and derive analytic criteria for efficient formation and long-term survival of the hydrogenic ground-state cloud, confronting them with current bounds on axion-photon couplings. We discuss observational implications of these PBH+cloud systems, including resonant axion-to-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres and finite-size microlensing distortions. In the former case, the resonance condition selects a conversion shell outside the neutron star surface, and we show that the large axion occupation number of the cloud can compensate for the small conversion probability. The resulting transient line flux densities can exceed nominal VLA and ALMA sensitivities in regions where the Galactic encounter rate is observationally relevant. Independently, when the cloud size becomes comparable to or larger than the Einstein radius, finite-size effects can modify the standard point-lens microlensing light curve.
papers.reason: Studies stimulated capture of axion dark matter around primordial black holes and transient line signals in magnetospheres, relevant for BSM portal searches.

papers.title: Technically Natural Baryogenesis with the QCD Axion
papers.abstract: The strong CP problem, dark matter, and the observed baryon abundance may all be connected dynamically through the QCD axion, though whether this connection is realized in Nature depends on additional degrees of freedom. We show that the required dynamics can arise from technically natural ingredients if multiple axions mix through the QCD anomaly. We review the connection between axion rotation and the baryon asymmetry, revisit the axiogenesis and kinetic-misalignment proposals, and derive new limits on their dynamics. Motivated by these considerations, naturalness and axion quality, we construct a realization in which mixing with additional axions both enhances the effective QCD axion field range through monodromy and dissipates excess rotational energy through mixing with a dark confining gauge sector, thereby avoiding overclosure. We study the resulting effective dynamics in several illustrative limits, uncovering phenomena that may arise more generally in multi-axion theories. We numerically evolve the full coupled system and show that it can simultaneously reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry and dark matter abundance within a predictive region of parameter space testable by near-future direct and indirect searches. Depending on the model parameters, either the QCD axion or the new heavy axion constitutes the dominant dark matter component. Successful baryogenesis favors a QCD axion decay constant near its current astrophysical lower bound, while the heavy axion lies within reach of forthcoming astrophysical and cosmological observations.
papers.reason: Discusses multi-axion dynamics for baryogenesis and dark matter, offering indirect connections to BSM cosmology.

papers.title: Auditing anapole dark matter: the limits of model independence in dark matter effective field theory
papers.abstract: Effective field theory is a powerful tool for studying the low-energy behavior of dark sector models without explicit dependence on the high-energy physics. However, bottom-up EFT analyses can miss important processes in UV completions that are relevant for dark matter production and detection. In this work we demonstrate explicitly that for Majorana dark matter coupled to the photon by the dimension-six anapole operator, different UV completions make qualitatively different predictions at high energy colliders, in the early universe, and in direct detection experiments. Additionally, we show that competitive, and in some cases, leading constraints on anapole dark matter can be derived by searching for signatures of additional particles in the UV completion rather than direct probes of the DM itself. We argue that the UV completions studied in this work have categorically different phenomenologies and that `model-independent' EFT constraints are not always applicable.
papers.reason: Examines limitations of EFT for anapole dark matter and importance of UV completions across colliders and direct detection.

papers.title: Signatures of Leptophilic Baryogenesis at Muon Colliders
papers.abstract: The baryon asymmetry of the Universe may be produced in a model with 3 Higgs fields, a Higgs Troika, without the need for a strong first order electroweak phase transition. The couplings of the new Higgs fields to Standard Model fermions are assumed in accord with the "Spontaneous Flavor Violation (SFV)" framework, in order to avoid large deviations from flavor physics constraints. We consider a leptophilic version of SFV and outline its potential signatures at future muon colliders, envisioned to be multi-TeV partonic center of momentum machines. Hence, they provide optimal venues to search for the leptophilic Higgs Troika baryogenesis mechanism. The projected reach for signals of the new scalars allows for probing the key components of the baryogenesis model at scales that accommodate cosmological requirements.
papers.reason: Studies leptophilic Higgs troika baryogenesis and its distinct signatures at future multi-TeV muon colliders.

papers.title: Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments
papers.abstract: We consider the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the recent 248 keV event observed by LZ and identify different experiments that could test it. Details of the underlying model and the ability of complementary experiments to test it depend significantly on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter distribution. We consider several example velocity distributions motivated by the impact of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) in order to map out the effects of this dependence. For example, we illustrate the type of high-velocity tail that would make the thermal Higgsino viable despite stringent constraints from solar neutrinos: Reducing the flux of the tail relative to simulation results improves the Higgsino fit, while extending the tail to higher velocities at fluxes below current simulation resolution evades the solar neutrino bound. This motivates more detailed simulations at higher resolution to understand the tail better. Even if xenon experiments confirm the signal event, complementary experiments are still required to test whether the underlying model is inelastic dark matter and to break degeneracies in the measurement of dark matter parameters such as mass and mass splitting. Heavy-element paleodetectors could cover most of the parameter space relevant to the LZ event. Their use of different elements could determine the dark matter mass and splitting, while their unique sensitivity to the history of the dark matter distribution could test the signal's LMC origin. Luminous detection in large neutrino detectors with heavy-element supplements could directly test the inelastic nature of the signal and measure the mass splitting, while its sensitivity to the radiative decay rate could provide strong evidence for the Higgsino interpretation.
papers.topic: Inelastic Dark Matter and Solar Neutrinos
papers.reason: Tests dark matter interpretations of the LZ anomaly against solar neutrino bounds and high-velocity tail velocity distributions.

papers.title: Two-variable longitudinal distribution of the $\Lambda_b$ in a three-quark light-front model
papers.abstract: We determine a normalized two-variable longitudinal distribution of the $\Lambda_b=(ud)b$ baryon from a covariant three-quark light-front wave function. The scalar $ud$ channel is selected with the good-component structure $C\gamma_5\gamma^+$, and the two independent transverse momenta are integrated without introducing an elementary diquark. The resulting model-scale valence distribution, $\Psi_2^{\rm LF}(x_u,x_d)$, retains both the heavy--light and internal-light momentum scales of the parent wave function. It is symmetric under $x_u\leftrightarrow x_d$, is concentrated where both light-quark fractions are small, and separates the total light-pair momentum from its internal sharing. For the central parameter set we find $\langle x_u\rangle=\langle x_d\rangle=0.130$, $\langle x_b\rangle=0.739$, $\langle\zeta^2\rangle=0.153$, and $\langle\zeta^4\rangle=0.055$, where $\zeta=(x_u-x_d)/(x_u+x_d)$. Parameter variations give $\langle x_u\rangle=0.130^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $\langle x_b\rangle=0.739^{+0.014}_{-0.014}$, $\langle\zeta^2\rangle=0.153^{+0.014}_{-0.016}$, and $\langle\zeta^4\rangle=0.055^{+0.009}_{-0.009}$. The heavy--light momentum partition is controlled mainly by $\beta_{b,ud}$ and $m_b$, whereas the internal $u$--$d$ sharing is most sensitive to $\beta_{ud}$. The result provides a compact finite-mass benchmark for three-quark longitudinal structure, with distinct observables for heavy--light momentum sharing and correlations inside the light pair.
papers.reason: Determines the two-variable longitudinal momentum distribution of the Lambda_b baryon using a covariant three-quark light-front wave function.

papers.title: Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons
papers.abstract: Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons probe nonperturbative gluodynamics, particularly the interplay between quark spin and gluonic excitations, and are of direct relevance to the search for exotic hadrons at Jefferson Lab. We calculate these transitions across the lowest charmonium-hybrid multiplet in a constituent gluon model based on Coulomb-gauge QCD in the heavy quark expansion. The results for $Y\to\eta_c\gamma$ and $Y\to \chi_{c0}\gamma$ overlap the width obtained in quenched lattice computations, whereas $\eta_{c1}\to J/\psi\gamma$ is substantially below the corresponding lattice estimate.
papers.reason: Calculates radiative transitions of hybrid charmonium in Coulomb-gauge QCD, relevant to exotic hadron searches at Jefferson Lab.

papers.title: From Axion Detection to Dark Matter Astronomy
papers.abstract: A global haloscope network could turn an axion discovery into astronomy of dark matter substructure and transients. We combine interferometric phase, spatial coherence, and spectroscopy to study the formation and evolution of axion substructure through measurements of flow directions and velocity distributions. For tidal streams, a four-site forecast shows how longitudinal and transverse velocity dispersions can be measured jointly. Interpreted with dynamical and population models, these measurements could test axion production scenarios. Extensions to miniclusters, axion stars, and emitted bursts would broaden the astrophysical reach of laboratory detection.
papers.reason: Examines how global haloscope networks can map dark matter substructure and velocity flows from axion direct detection signals.

papers.title: Dark Matter Particle Explorer: Ten-Year On-Orbit Performance and Scientific Outcomes
papers.abstract: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE, also known as ``Wukong'') is the first scientific space mission within the framework of the Strategic Pioneer Program on Space Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The main scientific objectives of DAMPE include indirect detection of dark matter, cosmic-ray physics, and high energy gamma-ray astronomy. Thanks to its large geometrical factor and thick imaging calorimeter, DAMPE could effectively detect cosmic-ray electrons (including positrons) and gamma-rays up to 10~TeV, and nuclei up to PeV. Since launched on 17 December 2015 into a Sun-synchronous orbit, DAMPE has been smoothly operating on orbit for more than ten years. Here we present an overview of instrument, on-orbit status, and highlight scientific results of DAMPE, including the measurements of the all-electron energy spectrum and the spectra of protons and other nuclei, and high energy gamma-ray line search.
papers.reason: Ten-year status and cosmic-ray electron/gamma results from the DAMPE space mission provide useful background on high-energy astroparticle environments.

papers.title: Collective Organization of String Fragmentation
papers.abstract: How coherent confining strings reorganize into hadronic matter is a central open problem in nonequilibrium gauge dynamics. Using real-time tensor-network simulations of the massive Schwinger model, we identify a collective organization underlying string fragmentation. For intermediate masses, the dynamics simplifies and more than $99\%$ of the temporal evolution of the electric-field probability distribution is governed by a single collective mode whose decay tracks the survival probability of the parent string. The extracted survival law exhibits the same Gaussian dependence implied by the Lund world-sheet area law, providing microscopic support for its characteristic area law dependence without assuming the Lund fragmentation mechanism. The same mode controls the transition from the coherent string to the produced mesons, explains the universal non-thermal effective fluid equation of state, and essentially controls the growth of bipartite entanglement through the causal propagation of massive pairs. These results identify collective fragmentation as an organizing principle of coherent string breaking and provide a microscopic perspective on the dynamical origin of a central ingredient of Lund hadronization.
papers.reason: Applies tensor networks to Schwinger model string fragmentation, providing microscopic insights into hadronization and Lund area laws.

papers.title: Four-dimensional QCD equation of state with a critical surface from contours of constant entropy density
papers.abstract: We present a new lattice-QCD-based equation of state in the four-dimensional space of $(T,\mu_B,\mu_Q,\mu_S)$ which features a critical surface. This is obtained by generalizing the expansion of constant entropy density contours across the multiple conserved charges of QCD. Since this expansion permits the presence of a first-order phase transition, this is the first lattice QCD based equation of state in four dimensions with a critical surface. We parametrize the chemical potential space using spherical coordinates $(\mu,\theta,\varphi)$, reducing the problem to a one-dimensional extrapolation in $(T,\mu)$ at fixed angles that, together, span the full 4D space. By integrating the extrapolated entropy density, we reconstruct the pressure, from which we obtain the conserved charge densities, their susceptibilities and the speed of sound. Our results agree quantitatively with other lattice QCD constructions at low chemical potentials in the crossover region, and predict the emergence of a first-order phase transition at higher chemical potentials. We study equation of state properties in detail under heavy-ion collision (HIC) conditions for the strangeness and electric charge densities ($n_S=0,~n_Q=0.4n_B$), where we find the CP location at $(T_c,\mu_{B,c},\mu_{Q,c},\mu_{S,c})=(115\pm7,646\pm72,-12\pm3,117\pm16)$ MeV. In particular, we find a strong non-monotonic dependence of baryon number susceptibilities along the chemical freeze-out line at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} \lesssim 7.7$ GeV. Finally, we outline further applications of the 4D equation of state, including charge-neutral matter relevant to neutron stars and large isospin density relevant to cosmic trajectories in the early Universe.
papers.reason: Constructs a 4D QCD equation of state with a critical surface from lattice QCD, relevant to heavy-ion collisions and high-density matter.

papers.title: Effective shear viscosity from the friction term in relativistic multi-fluid hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Within a three-fluid description of heavy-ion collisions, we investigate how nuclear friction can be used to model shear stress. In this multi-fluid approach, the individual fluids (projectile, target and fireball) are each treated as locally equilibrated ideal fluids at all times, while the local energy-momentum tensor of the superposed system exhibits characteristic anisotropies in its Landau rest frame. From the corresponding non-vanishing shear stress densities and the gradients of the Landau velocity field, we infer an ``effective shear viscosity'' according to the Navier-Stokes relation. We present the time evolution of the resulting values of $\eta_{\rm eff}$ and the generated entropy density in nuclear collisions at different beam energies ($1.23\,A\text{GeV} \le E_{\mathrm{lab}} \le 29.7\,A\text{GeV}$). The resulting dimensionless ratio $\eta_{\rm eff}/s$ is determined dynamically and self-consistently within the non-equilibrium friction model. We discuss the relation to previous calculations using alternative methods in hydrodynamics and to estimates based on microscopic transport models.
papers.reason: Computes effective shear viscosity dynamically from nuclear friction in relativistic multi-fluid heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: CT25: the new generation of CTEQ-TEA PDFs
papers.abstract: This contribution reviews CT25, a new generation of CTEQ--TEA parton distribution functions (PDFs) for precision QCD. With its first member sets released in 2025, the CT25 family addresses common uses of parton distributions in diverse contexts. We describe the CTEQ--TEA Parton Cloud, an online database of exploratory global fits to precision QCD measurements, from which we select PDF solutions for general- and special-purpose calculations. These solutions are published as complementary error PDF ensembles---the baseline CT25, CT25m, CT25pd, and ensembles with conservative priors---optimized for distinct uses. They implement new approaches to quantifying uncertainties and different treatments of theoretical, parametrization, and nuclear-target uncertainties. In particular, they provide complementary frameworks for exploring PDF uncertainties at large partonic momentum fractions relevant to HL-LHC and EIC studies. Further details will appear in the forthcoming CT25 publication.
papers.reason: Reviews new CTEQ-TEA global PDF fits with novel treatments of nuclear-target and high-$x$ uncertainties.

papers.title: Nonleptonic decays of the double-charmed baryon $\Xi_{cc}^{+}$ with dynamically determined baryon wave functions
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent observation of the double-charmed baryon $\Xi_{cc}^{+}$ by the LHCb Collaboration, we systematically investigate the two-body nonleptonic decays of the $\Xi_{cc}^{+}$ into a single-charmed baryon and a light pseudoscalar meson. In our calculation, both factorizable and nonfactorizable decay amplitudes are evaluated within the framework of nonrelativistic quark model combined with the baryon wave functions dynamically determined by numerically solving the three-body Schr\"{o}dinger equation with a nonrelativistic potential model. In particular, the nonfactorizable $W$-exchange amplitudes are estimated under pole model by considering $J^{P}=1/2^{\pm}$ low-lying intermediate charmed-baryon poles, and our results show that these contributions are comparable to or even dominate the factorizable amplitudes in several decay channels. Moreover, assuming a lifetime of $\tau_{\Xi_{cc}^{+}}=47~\text{fs}$, we predict relatively large branching fractions for several CF decays, including $\mathcal{B}(\Xi_{cc}^{+}\to\Xi_{c}^{\prime0}\pi^{+})=8.90\%$, $\mathcal{B}(\Xi_{cc}^{+}\to\Omega_{c}^{0}K^{+})=7.09\%$, $\mathcal{B}(\Xi_{cc}^{+}\to\Sigma_{c}^{+}\bar{K}^{0})=6.92\%$, $\mathcal{B}(\Xi_{cc}^{+}\to\Xi_{c}^{+}\pi^{0})=5.28\%$, and $\mathcal{B}(\Xi_{cc}^{+}\to\Sigma_{c}^{++}K^{-})=5.17\%$. These channels are promising candidates for future experimental searches at the LHCb.
papers.reason: Evaluates nonleptonic decays of Xi_cc+ baryons using potential models and dynamically determined three-body wave functions.

papers.title: Algebraic coefficients of fractional parentage for three particles in the oscillator Jacobi basis
papers.abstract: We present a closed-form construction of the orbital coefficients of fractional parentage (CFP) of three identical particles in the translationally invariant harmonic oscillator (HO) Jacobi basis. These are usually obtained by numerically diagonalizing a permutation operator in every energy-angular-momentum block. We show this diagonalization is unnecessary. Dressing the class operator $P_{13} + P_{23}$ with the single unitary $W = H^1 \Phi$ -- a fixed complexification followed by the HO bracket with mass parameter $d=1$ -- turns it into the label swap times an integer. Every CFP is then the single ket $|K_{i,s}\rangle = 2Q^s W^\dagger|i\rangle$ -- a 2-scaled, sign-decorated column of the $d=1$ bracket restricted to one $e_2$-parity of the labels -- whose norm, $1 + s\langle i | J | i \rangle$, is itself a single matrix element. The same $W$ carries label parity into swap symmetry, $W Q^s W^\dagger = R^s$, making the bookkeeping collapse. The eigenvalues are exact integers $\pm 2$ and $\pm 1$ labeling the $S(3)$ symmetry classes. The construction is uniform in $E$, $L$ and symmetry class, reducing CFP-specific work from $O(n^3)$ to $O(n^2)$ in block dimension. An eigensolver remains only inside the bracket engine supplying $H^1$, where all residual numerical error originates. We implement this on an SU(3)-basis bracket engine, checking all 1301 blocks up to $E=50$ (912 366 CFPs, largest block $2907 \times 2907$): the $S(3)$ class assignment is exact everywhere. The residual numerical error (entirely the bracket engine's) stays below $10^{-8}$ for $E \leq 35$, restoring to $\leq 10^{-22}$ via a quadruple-precision build beyond that. We further validate against independently generated antisymmetrization data of a production three-nucleon code, including the $^3$He ground-state energy.
papers.reason: Presents an algebraic, closed-form construction of coefficients of fractional parentage for three particles in harmonic oscillator bases.

papers.title: Non-Invertible Froggatt-Nielsen Symmetry
papers.abstract: We investigate non-invertible completions of anomalous flavor symmetries and their application to Dirac neutrino masses. We formulate symmetry defects dressed by topological quantum field theories for flavor symmetries including finite non-Abelian flavor transformations with rational anomaly characters and modular flavor symmetries with the rational part of modular anomaly cocycles, for gauge sectors with the required exact higher-form symmetry. As a concrete example, we construct a Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) model in which an order-four subgroup $\mathbb Z_4^{\rm FN}\subset U(1)_{\rm FN}$ is completed into a non-invertible defect through its mixed anomaly with an intermediate hidden $U(1)_H$ gauge sector in the infrared monopole-decoupling limit. The non-invertible FN symmetry can be explicitly broken at the energy scale where monopoles become dynamical. This breaking from the infrared viewpoint can be realized in an ultraviolet hidden $SU(2)_H$ theory as instanton effects, where a constrained instanton with topological charge one generates a fermion mixing term that violates FN charge by one unit. Its coefficient contains the nonperturbative factor $\zeta_H\sim\exp[-8\pi^2/g_H^2(v_H)]$. When independent FN-breaking terms are subleading, integrating out the heavy fermions gives $(Y_\nu)_{ij}\propto\zeta_H\epsilon^{\ell_i+n_j}$ in a rotated basis for the right-handed neutrinos, to leading order in the instanton-induced fermion mixing. The nonperturbative factor provides the exponential suppression of the neutrino Yukawa couplings, while the FN charges determine the powers of $\epsilon$. For the chosen FN charges and generic order-one coefficients, $m_2/m_3\sim\epsilon$, favoring normal ordering. An independent $\mathbb Z_8^D$ gauge symmetry forbids Majorana masses. The same FN charge assignment reproduces the leading quark and charged-lepton Yukawa hierarchies.
papers.reason: Constructs non-invertible completions of flavor symmetries and applies them to Dirac neutrino mass textures via instanton effects.

papers.title: Multi-Higgs production from a theory of varying Higgs quartic and top Yukawa couplings
papers.abstract: We study the collider phenomenology of a theory in which the Higgs quartic self-coupling and the top Yukawa coupling are \textit{varying couplings}, which arise dynamically from two scalar fields, $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$. Depending on the scalar masses relative to twice the top-quark mass, the heavy scalars decay mainly to Higgs boson pairs ($hh$) or to top-quark pairs ($t\bar t$), giving two distinct signatures. We find sizeable cross sections for resonant $hh$ production, and also for the background-suppressed process with three Higgs bosons ($hhh$) from associated production, $pp \to h\phi_i \to hhh$. By recasting ATLAS resonance searches, we set bounds on the effective new-physics scales $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ at the TeV scale. We also show that the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) will probe this parameter space further, through combined measurements of the $hh$, $t\bar t$ and multi-Higgs channels. This gives a strong, multi-channel test of whether the electroweak sector has a dynamical origin.
papers.reason: Collider phenomenology of varying Higgs quartic and top Yukawa couplings leading to multi-Higgs and top final states.

papers.title: One generation of the Standard Model as a quantum error-correcting code
papers.abstract: Together with a right-handed neutrino, the fermions of one generation of the Standard Model are labelled by five bits, a combinatorial structure tied to anomaly cancellation. We make this precise. Anomaly cancellation is the vanishing of a cubic form, the defining property of triorthogonal codes, the quantum error-correcting codes behind magic state distillation. Removing the right-handed neutrino gives a $[[15,1,3]]_p$ code for every prime $p$, including the Bravyi-Kitaev code for $p = 2$. For qutrits it is the unique shortest distance-three triorthogonal code.
papers.reason: Examines fermion generations of the Standard Model and anomaly cancellation as triorthogonal quantum error-correcting codes.

papers.title: Lossy Lorentz boosts at ultra-relativistic energies: Numerical study and source survey of high-energy physics software
papers.abstract: Most high-energy-physics software packages implement Lorentz boosts for themselves. At sufficiently large boosts, these routines can return finite, plausible-looking four-vectors whose invariant masses and rest-frame properties are no longer accurate. We survey implementations in widely used collider and air-shower software and compare representative algorithms in three numerical tests. We find that the main problem is usually information discarded by the representation, rather than the arithmetic of the boost formula. Information can be lost when a boost is specified only by its velocity, and again when the result is stored only through Cartesian components. Richer boost input prevents the first loss, while retaining light-cone coordinates prevents the second. Ordinary hard processes at present colliders are safe in double precision; the relevant regimes are low-mass systems, highly boosted auxiliary frames, single-precision particle records and air-shower simulations. Extreme scale hierarchies in parton-shower accuracy tests and ultra-heavy particle decays provide still more demanding cases.
papers.topic: Lossy Lorentz Boosts in HEP Software
papers.reason: Examines numerical precision loss in Lorentz boost implementations across high-energy physics and air-shower software packages.

papers.title: Probing the Axion--Photon--Dark Photon Interaction with LHC Mono-Photons and Fermi-LAT Gamma-Ray Lines
papers.abstract: We investigate the axion--photon--dark photon interaction at the LHC and in gamma-ray line searches. By recasting the CMS mono-photon data, we derive a $95\%$ CL exclusion reaching $g_{a\gamma'\gamma}\simeq4.8\times10^{-4}\ {\rm GeV}^{-1}$ for dark photon masses $m_{\gamma'}\lesssim100$ GeV, with sensitivity extending to $m_{\gamma'}\simeq2.3$ TeV, where the effective theory approaches its validity limit. This improves upon the existing LEP mono-photon constraint by a factor of $3$ or more, depending on the dark photon mass. The projected HL-LHC sensitivity improves by a further factor of $\sim2.7$ and extends the reach to $m_{\gamma'}\simeq3$ TeV. The same interaction also induces $s$-wave annihilation of axions into $\gamma\gamma$. If the axion constitutes dark matter, Fermi-LAT gamma-ray line data become more constraining than the LHC for $m_a\gtrsim160$ GeV at $m_{\gamma'}=300$ GeV, where the on-shell collider signal is kinematically suppressed. Combining collider and gamma-ray line constraints excludes a thermal relic axion across the axion mass range considered for this benchmark.
papers.reason: Derives collider and gamma-ray line constraints on axion-photon-dark photon couplings using CMS mono-photons and Fermi-LAT.

papers.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
papers.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.
papers.reason: Introduces a multi-agent framework to translate quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows (Schwinger and NJL models), offering an interesting AI workflow tool.

papers.title: All three-loop four-point massless integrals with one off-shell leg
papers.abstract: We present the complete set of massless three-loop four-point master integrals with one off-shell external leg. These are essential building blocks for the three-loop virtual corrections to Higgs-boson or vector-boson production in association with a jet at the Large Hadron Collider, required for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD predictions. We construct a complete basis of canonical integrals by identifying integrands with simple poles and unit leading singularities, solely by integrand analysis. This includes an integral family with 371 master integrals and a 19-dimensional top sector. The solutions for all relevant integrals are provided as a map to a minimal set of iterated integrals graded according to their analytic properties, together with high-precision series expansions.
papers.reason: Computes master integrals for NN-N-NLO QCD corrections at colliders, useful for high-precision precision backgrounds.

papers.title: Bounds on hadronic contributions to the anomalous magnetic moment of the $\tau$ lepton from QCD Sum Rules
papers.abstract: A QCD sum-rule study is performed to place bounds on the leading-order (LO) hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the $\tau$ lepton ($a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO},\, a_\tau = (g-2)_\tau/2$). The QCD contributions to $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$ are modeled as a combination of Laplace QCD sum rules (LSRs) and finite-energy QCD sum rules (FESRs) of various weights, which are bounded by H\"older and related fundamental inequalities. The light-quark ($u,\,d,\,s$) contributions are evaluated up to five-loop order in perturbative contributions in the chiral limit, LO in light quark mass corrections, next-to-leading order (NLO) in dimension-four QCD condensates and to LO in dimension-six QCD condensates. Extending previous work on $a_\mu^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$, we present a robust methodology for using QCD sum rules to constrain $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$, and more generally any lepton $g-2$. A criterion is developed to extract from the bounds analysis a final result of $a_\tau^\mathrm{QCD} = \left( 3.385\pm 0.048 \right) \times 10^{-6}$, which after inclusion of charmonium and bottomonium contributions gives a final result $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO} = \left( 3.501\pm0.048\right) \times 10^{-6}$, comparable to data-driven and lattice predictions. Lattice QCD results along with our value for $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$ are used to obtain a combined QCD determination from lattice and sum-rule methods of $a_\mu^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO} = (7.217\pm0.233)\times10^{-8}$. Our analysis provides fundamental QCD sum-rule inputs into the theoretical determinations of $a_\tau$, and establishes new methodologies for QCD sum-rule determinations of low-energy observables.
papers.reason: Applies QCD sum rules to constrain hadronic vacuum polarization for lepton magnetic moments.

papers.title: Two-loop HTL-resummed thermodynamics for pure $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: We compute the two-loop hard-thermal-loop (HTL) resummed thermodynamic potential of pure four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory using regularization by dimensional reduction. Our result is gauge invariant and was renormalized using vacuum energy, gluon mass $m_d$ and quark mass $m_q$ counterterms. The thermal mass parameters are determined self-consistently and numerically from gap equations incorporating the running coupling. Based on these solutions, we numerically calculate the scaled pressure, entropy density, energy density, and trace anomaly and compare them with the results in the static perturbative limit through $\mathcal O(\lambda^2)$. For the first three quantities, next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections are positive and have discernible effects at small coupling, and reduce the renormalization-scale dependence at relatively large couplings. We assess $m_q$-prescription dependence by comparing these results with those obtained by setting $m_q=0$. We find that it has a substantial impact on $m_d$ and the scalar mass $m_s$ at large couplings, and it reverses the signs of the NLO corrections to the first three quantities and qualitatively alters the trace anomaly.
papers.reason: Computes two-loop HTL thermodynamics for supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory.

papers.title: PTagent: An LLM-assisted tool for finite-temperature model construction in cosmological phase transitions
papers.abstract: Cosmological phase-transition calculations require well-defined finite-temperature numerical models, whose construction involves assembling model information under consistent theoretical prescriptions. In this work we present \texttt{PTagent}, a large language model (LLM) agent-based framework for constructing such models from SARAH model files, research papers, and DRalgo sources. The LLM agent interprets and organizes model information and identifies unresolved physical choices, while dedicated backends perform the model-dependent calculations. After review and approval of the resulting physical model specification, the backends generate the corresponding CosmoTransitions-style or PhaseTracer-style numerical potentials. By separating model interpretation from numerical implementation, PTagent provides an inspectable and reproducible approach to finite-temperature model construction for cosmological phase-transition studies.
papers.reason: Introduces an LLM agent framework for constructing finite-temperature cosmological phase transition models, aligning with interest in ML/AI workflows.

papers.title: Determining the Threshold Excess in Top-Quark Pair Production through a Global PDF Analysis
papers.abstract: We present an empirical determination of the threshold excess $\Delta$ in top-quark pair production, taking full account of correlated uncertainties with PDFs, the top-quark mass $m_t$ and the strong coupling $\alpha_s(m_Z)$. We extract $\Delta$ from a variety of differential $t\bar{t}$ cross-section measurements by ATLAS and CMS at 8 and 13 TeV, using theoretical predictions of the $t\bar{t}$ continuum up to NNLO QCD accuracy, including an estimate of missing higher order uncertainties and NLO EW corrections. At 8 TeV we see no evidence of a significant threshold excess, but at 13 TeV obtain results above the NNLO QCD $t\bar{t}$ background at just over two $\sigma$ when we combine all the available measurements. We also find evidence of a strong correlation between $\Delta$ and $m_t$, which must be taken into account if the uncertainty on any threshold excess is to be estimated reliably.
papers.reason: Global PDF analysis of threshold excesses in top-quark pair production.

papers.title: Revisiting $B_c^{(*)}$ production in $Z$-boson decays at NLO in QCD
papers.abstract: We study $B_c^{(*)}$ production in $Z$-boson decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD within the color-singlet nonrelativistic QCD framework. The analysis covers both the $1S$ and $2S$ pseudoscalar and vector states, extending the phenomenological study to radially excited $B_c$ mesons. We calculate direct production widths and energy-fraction and invariant-mass distributions, including both charm- and bottom-quark production topologies.
